description: self-fix.sh's one-fixer-per-loop guard is a permanent block, not a bounded retry: if the spawned Opus session ever hangs (crashes into a stalled tool call, runs out of context, or itself produces a stuck interactive state inside its own detached tmux pane — the exact same class of bug flagged in FIND-001/002 but for the FIXER itself), `tmux has-session` stays true indefinitely. Every future self-fix.sh call for that loop then silently no-ops forever with no timeout, no escalation, and no automatic recovery.

evidence.snippet: if tmux -S "$SOCK" has-session -t "$SESSION" 2>/dev/null; then echo "$(date '+%F %T') self-fix[$LOOP] already running — skip" >> "$LOG"; echo "self-fix[$LOOP] already running"; exit 0; fi

concreteFailureScenario: The self-fix Opus session for 'reddit' gets stuck (e.g. mid-CDP call it cannot resolve). Every subsequent day, reddit-loop's STEP0 calls self-fix.sh again for the same blocker; each call sees the stale tmux session as 'already running' and skips, forever. The only way out is a human manually killing `/tmp/anicca-selffix-reddit-tmux.sock` — reintroducing exactly the human-babysitting dependency the claim says does not exist.
